summary: This benchmark evaluates how camera baseline orientation affects stereo matching disambiguation in the presence of periodic textures. Using a controlled synthetic setup with horizontal period-3 textures, the authors show that an orthogonal (perpendicular) camera baseline resolves 97.09% of depth aliasing ties between depths 1 and 4 that collinear baselines cannot break. The methodology and controls are mathematically sound, though the scope is strictly synthetic and brief.
strengths: Rigorous experimental controls, including an opposite horizontal baseline and a mismatched perpendicular baseline to rule out uninformative baseline artifacts.
Precise geometric formulation isolating the 1D aperture and periodicity problem in stereo matching.
Includes rigorous statistical evaluation, reporting exact counts (3,939 of 4,057 pairs) and layout-paired 95% confidence intervals (+96.30% to +97.84%).
Clear acknowledgement of limitations regarding transferability to real-world natural images and continuous disparity representations.
weaknesses: Evaluated purely on synthetic, discrete-shift grid textures without validation on realistic scenes, non-integer disparities, or continuous sensor noise.
Very brief manuscript (522 words) lacking detailed discussion of prior multi-baseline camera array configurations (e.g., cross or T-shaped baselines).
suggestions: Extend the benchmark to test fractional subpixel disparities and varied spatial frequencies to quantify degradation boundaries.
Discuss practical multi-camera rigs (such as cross-baseline or L-shaped camera arrays) and compare against classical multi-baseline stereo literature.

claims.text: With texture repeating every three horizontal pixels, depths 1 and 4 produced identical local matches in both horizontal camera directions.
When two images are used, their per-level costs are added before selecting the lowest-cost depth.
The perpendicular view recovered both correct depths on 3,939 of 4,057 aligned pixel pairs.
claims.source: Internal experimental audit and mathematical consistency of non-periodic vertical texture matching under y-axis shifts

novelty_vs_existing.title: A Multiple-Baseline Stereo System
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Okutomi and Kanade demonstrated ambiguity reduction via multiple baselines along camera displacement lines; this submission specifically benchmarks an orthogonal baseline isolating 1D periodic texture degeneracy where collinear baselines strictly fail.
